messages:
ashley: Heads-up — sudden spike in GPU preempts in ap-southeast1 starting ~04:12 UTC. Grafana shows eviction rate x3. https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/abcd123/evictions
mike: link?
ashley: https://grafana.internal/redwood/d/abcd123/evictions?panelId=7 . Lots of small pods landing on dedicated racks and then big gang jobs get preempted.
jia: we rolled taint `compute:new:v2` earlier. some helm charts still emit `compute:new` (legacy). Could be toleration-version mismatch.
mike: also noticing tiny sidecars with nodeAffinity nvlink==present getting packed on the same nodes as large inference gangs. binpacking policy ended up fragmenting racks.
nate: checking scheduler bind logs and admission: `grep -i "toleration" /var/log/admission | tail` — several admissions changed toleration format during the rollout.
(nate paste) `admission: pod inference-2023 accepted tolerations=[compute:new]` — older CI jobs.
ashley: scheduler appears to treat unversioned toleration as "matches" compute:new:v2 for now, so pods without explicit v2 toleration still land on dedicated nodes. when autoscaler drains, it preempts by gang -> cascade.
jia: action: pause taint rollout, and add admission webhook to reject unversioned tolerations. I'll open rollback PR.
mike: we should also add a policy to the cluster-autoscaler to prefer packing tiny pods onto general-purpose racks (annotation `binpack-preference: general`) so we don't co-locate tiny sidecars with large-gang nodes.
ashley: rolling rollback started on ap-southeast1 pools (a/c) now.
sre-bot: deploy-bot: rollback job kicked for taint-rollout-2026 on ap-southeast1-a -> ap-southeast1-c
nate: evictions trending back down within ~90s after rollback. cost anomaly reducing.
jia: followups: 1) infra#789 create admission-level check for toleration format, 2) patch helm charts for legacy jobs, 3) autoscaler annotation to steer tiny pods, 4) add e2e that simulates mixed toleration versions + gang scheduling.
mike: propose alert: `gpu_eviction_rate{region="ap-southeast1"} > 0.4` for 5m to P0 oncall. catch earlier next time.
ashley: good catch everyone — i'll update the incident thread and ping support to notify impacted customers.
